subject: Life Skills
title: Temptation Bundling
description: A micro-lesson that makes Temptation Bundling usable.

hook.text: She only allowed herself to listen to her favorite podcast while running. Within a month, she ran every day.

buildup.text: Wharton professor Katy Milkman named this 'temptation bundling' — pairing a want with a should to motivate action.

discovery.text: The key is restriction. The reward must only be available during the dreaded task, not anytime you want it.

twist.text: It works best for tasks that are boring, not emotionally threatening. Deep anxiety needs a different fix.

climax.text: Match your best guilty pleasure to your worst chore. Laundry plus a show. Spreadsheets plus fancy coffee.

punchline.text: Pair the chore with the treat. Both win.

quiz.question: What makes temptation bundling effective?
options: The reward is only available during the dreaded task
You reward yourself after completing the task
It works equally for all types of procrastination
